correctness.rationale: For \(S=x+y\), the exact equation \(\dot S=a-x\) and arbitrary antiderivative tests give \(\mathbb E[x\mid S]=a\). Orthogonality of \(x-a\) to functions of \(S\) gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(x,S)=0\), hence \(\operatorname{Cov}(x,y)=-\operatorname{Var}(x)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(y)=\operatorname{Var}(S)+\operatorname{Var}(x)\). Arbitrary antiderivative tests in \(x\) give \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=((b+1)x-a)/x^2\), whose residual is exactly \(\dot x/x^2\). Compact positivity makes the normalization integrable and forces the strict support barrier. Zero \(x\)- or \(S\)-variance forces the unique equilibrium, so the non-equilibrium inequalities are strict. The packaged checker verifies the algebraic and covariance reductions.

value.rationale: The Brusselator is a canonical two-species chemical oscillator in which the sum \(x+y\) is the natural total intermediate concentration and the \(x\)-nullcline organizes the phase plane. The accepted theorem gives both objects exact stationary-statistical meanings: every total-concentration fiber has the same activator mean \(a\), while every activator fiber has inhibitor mean exactly on the nullcline. This immediately forces a universal negative covariance and a strict variance ordering for every non-equilibrium stationary regime, independent of orbit period or phase. These are directly testable constraints for periodic or stationary simulation data and are stronger than known global means or phase-portrait statements.
